info.title: Valendata REST API
info.description: Create, run, schedule, and improve skills and workflows over JSON and HTTPS. Every route is under `/v1`; changes inside v1 are additive only (new routes, new optional parameters, new response fields). A route that will go away is marked `deprecated` here and answers with `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and a `Link` to its replacement for at least six months before it is removed. Errors, limits, pagination and idempotency: https://docs.valendata.com/api-reference/errors.

get.description: Your credit balance (exact, as a decimal string), plan and monthly allowance, the low-credit flag, auto-recharge, and your workspaces. Needs `account:read`.

post.description: Save a website login for your skills to sign in with. Stored encrypted in your Vault, never shared with your workspace, never returned. Needs a session or an API key with `logins:write`.

get.description: Your saved logins, masked. Needs `logins:write`.
One saved login, masked: the site, a hint of the username, its label and notes, and whether it has an authenticator seed. Needs `logins:write`.

patch.description: Send a new password, username or authenticator seed. Nothing secret comes back.

delete.description: Deletes the login. Skills that signed in with it stop doing so.

get.description: Any run, skill or workflow: its status, and the result once it has finished. Skill runs hold their rows in `rows`; workflow runs hold `outputs` and have `kind: "workflow"`. Needs `runs:read` for a skill run, `workflows:read` for a workflow run.

post.description: Stop a queued or running run you started: a skill run, or a workflow run and what it is running inside. Rows already produced are kept. A finished run is left as it is (`cancelled: false`). Needs `skills:invoke` for a skill run, `workflows:invoke` for a workflow run.

When a site texts a sign-in code, the run waits up to 3 minutes for it. Send it here; the run types it into the page and carries on. Only the account that started the run. Needs `logins:use` on an API key.

get.description: Every schedule you may see, skills' and workflows'. `kind` narrows it to `skill` or `workflow`. A kind your key has no read scope for is left out.

schema.title: Response Get Schedule Api V1 Schedules  Schedule Id  Get

get.description: One schedule. Skill schedule ids start with `sklsch_`, workflow schedule ids with `wfsch_`.

patch.description: Change `cron` or `every`, `timezone`, `inputs`, `enabled`, or (skill schedules only) `max_results`. Only what you send changes. Needs `skills:write` or `workflows:write`; switching a workflow schedule on also needs `workflows:invoke`.

schema.title: Response Update Schedule Api V1 Schedules  Schedule Id  Patch

delete.description: Turn the schedule off and forget its settings. The skill or workflow stays.

parameters.name: status

schema.description: Comma-separated statuses, e.g. needs_fix,failed; active = queued, recording and validating.
schema.title: Status

parameters.description: Comma-separated statuses, e.g. needs_fix,failed; active = queued, recording and validating.

200.description: A page of your skill creations.

get.description: Your skill creations, newest first, each as `GET /v1/skill-creations/{creation_id}` answers it (without `sample_rows`). Filter with `status` — a comma list, or `active` for every creation still in progress (`queued`, `recording`, `validating`) — and page with `limit` (1–100, default 20) and `cursor`. Only your own creations are listed.

Where a creation is: `queued`, `recording`, `validating`, `ready` (run `run_url`), `needs_fix` (the recording was saved as a draft skill with `sample_rows`, but its test replay did not pass — fix it with `POST /v1/skills/{slug}/improve`, do not create it again) or `failed` (nothing was saved; `error` says why). `progress` is the latest step in plain words and `credits_charged` what the creation has cost so far. `next_step` says what to do. Only the account that started it can read it.

Where an improvement is: `queued`, `working`, `validating`, `done` (`result` and `improved` say whether the new version is live; `changes` shows each field before → after; `details` shows new, merged and unclear fields) or `failed` (`error`). The account that started it and anyone who can edit the Skill (its owner or a workspace editor) can poll it; anyone else gets 404.

Your skills and those shared into your workspaces, newest first: each with its inputs, health over the last 20 runs, last run, and the routes to run it. Search with `q`, filter by `status`, and page with `limit` (1–100, default 50) and `cursor`. Needs `skills:read`.

schema.description: Text in the name, slug or description
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Text in the name, slug or description

post.description: Record `task` in a cloud browser from `start_url` and publish it as a Skill. Answers at once with a creation id; poll `GET /v1/skill-creations/{creation_id}`. Up to 2 recordings in progress per account; needs at least 10 credits. Recordings cannot sign in to websites.

202.description: Creation started (or the existing one, for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

post.description: Older form of `POST /v1/skills/{slug}/run` that takes `skill_id` and `parameters` in the body. It still works. New code should use the slug route.

parameters.name: max_results

schema.description: Max rows to return; 0 means the entire list. Omit to use the skill's saved default.
schema.title: Max Results

parameters.description: Max rows to return; 0 means the entire list. Omit to use the skill's saved default.

get.description: The skill and its contract: `input_schema`, `output_json_schema`, `reliability`, versions, and fast path. A public skill needs no key. A private skill returns 404 to anyone who may not run it.

patch.description: Change a skill's name, description, inputs, output fields, run settings, saved login, or sharing. Only what you send changes. Answers with the skill as `GET /v1/skills/{slug}` returns it, plus `changes`, `warnings`, and `login`. Owner or workspace editor; `login_id` and `visibility` are owner only. Needs `skills:write` (and `logins:write` for `login_id`).

delete.description: Delete a skill you own. Its runs are kept (your billing history) and its schedule stops. If a workflow uses the skill, you get `409` listing those workflows, unless you pass `force=true`. Needs `skills:write`.

parameters.name: force

schema.description: Delete even though workflows use it (their step then fails)
schema.title: Force

parameters.description: Delete even though workflows use it (their step then fails)

get.description: Success rate and repairs over the last 20 runs, when it last worked, the last failure kind, the live recipe version, and each route's health. Public for public Skills; private Skills return 404 to anyone who may not run them.

post.description: Change a Skill in one of three modes. `fix` (default): relearn it from a plain-English hint about where the data is. `add_fields`: capture new fields you describe in plain English; the request is first compared with the Skill's fields, so a re-worded duplicate is merged into the existing field and an unclear one comes back as a question. `relearn_details`: rebuild how the Skill opens each result (its per-row detail steps), for when the site changed or detail fields come back empty. Every mode runs on a cloud browser, saves a new recipe version and checks it with a short run (up to 5 rows). The new version stays live only if it is better; otherwise it is kept as a candidate and the previous recipe stays live. Owner or workspace editor only; drafts allowed. One improvement at a time per account and per Skill, up to 6 an hour, at least 10 credits to start. Charged to the caller.

202.description: Improvement started (or the existing one, for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

get.description: The Skill's full change history, newest first: every fix, added field and re-learn by anyone allowed to edit it (the owner or a workspace editor), from any channel (`source`), plus past Refine and Re-learn entries imported from before (`imported: true`, `result: applied`).

200.description: The Skill's change history, newest first.

put.description: `{"version": n}` pins the Skill to version `n`; `{"version": null}` unpins it. While pinned, automatic repairs are saved as candidate versions and do not change what runs. Owner or workspace editor only.

post.description: Run a published Skill and wait for the rows. Put the Skill's inputs at the top level of the JSON body (or in the query string). The body keys `browser_type`, `proxy_config`, `profile_id`, `scrape_mode`, `max_pages`, and `version` are run settings, not inputs. Inputs are checked against `input_schema` before anything runs. If too many of your runs are in progress, this returns 429 with `Retry-After` instead of waiting.

schema.description: Max rows to return; 0 means the entire list. Omit to use the skill's saved default.

schema.description: The skill's inputs at the top level, plus optional run settings: max_pages, version, browser_type, proxy_config, profile_id, scrape_mode.

post.description: Validate the inputs, start the run, and answer at once with a `run_id`. If your account is at its limit of runs in progress, the run queues. Poll `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` or pass `webhook_url`.

202.description: Run queued (or the existing one, for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

get.description: A skill's runs, newest first. Filter by `status` (comma-separated) and `since`; page with `limit` (1–100, default 50) and `cursor`. The owner and workspace see every run; someone running a public skill sees their own. Needs `runs:read`.

parameters.name: since

schema.description: Only runs started at or after this time
schema.title: Since

parameters.description: Only runs started at or after this time

get.description: The skill's schedule, as a list of zero or one: a skill has one schedule. Needs `skills:read`.

post.description: Run a skill on a schedule. Give exactly one of `cron` or `every`, a `timezone`, the `inputs` each run uses (checked now), and `max_results` (default 100). `409` if the skill already has a schedule: change it with `PATCH /v1/schedules/{schedule_id}`. Each run spends the owner's credits. Needs `skills:write`.

get.description: Every recipe version, newest first, with which one is live and which is pinned. Needs the right to run the Skill.

schema.title: Response Diff Versions V1 Skills  Slug  Versions  A  Diff  B  Get

get.description: What changed from version `a` to version `b`.

post.description: Make version `n` the live recipe. The restore is saved as a new version. Owner or workspace editor only.

get.description: Credits spent per UTC day and per source between `from` and `to` (default the last 30 days, at most 366). Refunds are taken off; goodwill refunds for old over-charges are reported separately in `goodwill_refunds`. Needs `account:read`.

The secret your webhook deliveries are signed with. Each delivery carries `X-Valendata-Timestamp` and `X-Valendata-Signature: v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<raw body>")>`. Needs the `webhooks:read` scope when called with an API key. For 24 hours after a rotation the signature header carries two comma-separated values, new first.

post.description: Replace the signing secret with a new random one and return it. The previous secret keeps signing deliveries (as a second comma-separated `v1=` value) until `previous_valid_until`, 24 hours from now. Needs the `webhooks:write` scope when called with an API key.

get.description: Older form of `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` for workflow runs. It still works. New code should use `/v1/runs/{run_id}`.

schema.title: Response Get Workflow Run V1 Workflow Runs  Run Id  Get

get.description: Workflows you own and those shared with you through a workspace, newest first. Search with `q`; page with `limit` (1–100, default 25) and `cursor`. Needs `workflows:read`.

post.description: Create a workflow from its inputs, steps, and connections. Every step, connection, skill or workflow reference, and `{{inputs.x}}` is checked first; a `422` lists every problem and nothing is saved. A key limited to some workflows cannot create one. Needs `workflows:write`.

get.description: A workflow and its contract: inputs, output shape, track record, routes, and its MCP tool name. `include_graph=true` adds its steps and connections.

parameters.name: include_graph

schema.description: Also return steps, connections and version.
schema.title: Include Graph

parameters.description: Also return steps, connections and version.

patch.description: Change a workflow's name, description, inputs, steps, or connections. Only what you send changes; `steps` replaces the whole list. The state before is kept as a version you can restore in the app. Owner or workspace owner, admin, or member. Needs `workflows:write`.

delete.description: Delete a workflow you own and take its schedule off. Its runs are kept and stay readable with GET /v1/runs/{run_id}. This cannot be undone. Needs `workflows:write`.

post.description: Checks the inputs against the workflow's declared inputs (a bad call is a 422 and costs nothing), runs it, and waits up to `wait` seconds (default 60, max 120). Finished in time → 200 with `outputs`. Still running → 202 with the run so far; poll its `status_url`. If your account is at its limit of runs in progress, the answer is 429 with `Retry-After` (use `/runs` to queue instead).

Checks the inputs, starts the run and answers at once with a `run_id`. If your account is at its limit of runs in progress, the run waits as `pending`. Poll `GET /v1/workflow-runs/{run_id}` or pass `webhook_url` to receive the finished run as a signed POST.

202.description: Run started (or the existing one, for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

get.description: A workflow's runs, newest first. Filter by `status`, `source`, `since`, and `until`; page with `limit` (1–100, default 25) and `cursor`. Needs `workflows:read`.

schema.description: One of: pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled.
schema.title: Status

parameters.description: One of: pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled.

get.description: The workflow's schedule, as a list of zero or one: a workflow has one schedule. Needs `workflows:read`.

post.description: Run a workflow on a schedule. Give exactly one of `cron` or `every`, a `timezone`, and the `inputs` each run gets. `409` if it already has one. Needs `workflows:write`, plus `workflows:invoke` to create it switched on.

ApiKeyAuth.description: API key with the `vd_sk_` prefix, as `Authorization: Bearer vd_sk_...`. Create keys in Settings → API Keys.

ApiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyHeader.description: The same API key in the `x-api-key` header.

X-Request-ID.description: This request's id (yours, if you sent a valid `X-Request-ID`). Quote it to support.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests a minute this API key may make.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current minute.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time (seconds) the current window ends.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the stored answer to an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.

Deprecation.description: When the route was deprecated (RFC 9745, `@<unix seconds>`).

Sunset.description: When the deprecated route may be removed (RFC 8594 HTTP-date).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Any unique string (such as your order id). Resending the same request with the same key within 24 hours returns the first answer (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and does nothing twice; the same key with a different request is a 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed: the body is not JSON, the cursor or Idempotency-Key is not valid.

example.detail: The request is malformed: the body is not JSON, the cursor or Idempotency-Key is not valid.

Unauthorized.description: The API key is missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

example.detail: The API key is missing, malformed, revoked, or expired.

PaymentRequired.description: Not enough credits to start. `detail` includes `current_balance` and `required`.

example.detail: Not enough credits to start. `detail` includes `current_balance` and `required`.

Forbidden.description: The key lacks a scope, is limited to other skills or workflows, or you may not do this.

example.detail: The key lacks a scope, is limited to other skills or workflows, or you may not do this.

NotFound.description: It does not exist, or it is not yours to see.

example.detail: It does not exist, or it is not yours to see.

Conflict.description: A conflict with the current state, or a request with this Idempotency-Key is still running.

example.detail: A conflict with the current state, or a request with this Idempotency-Key is still running.

Unprocessable.description: A field is invalid (`param` names it), or the Idempotency-Key was used with a different request.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests for this key, or too many runs in progress. Wait `Retry-After` seconds.

example.detail: Too many requests for this key, or too many runs in progress. Wait `Retry-After` seconds.

InternalError.description: Something broke on our side. Retry; runs that fail on our side are refunded.

example.detail: Something broke on our side. Retry; runs that fail on our side are refunded.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as ?cursor= for the next page; null on the last page.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: True when there is a next page (next_cursor is not null).

cancelled.title: Cancelled
cancelled.description: A stop was requested now (false: it had already finished)

stopped.title: Stopped
stopped.description: A workflow run: what it was running inside that was stopped too

every.title: Every
every.description: Instead of cron: hourly, daily, weekly, daily:HH:MM, weekly:<mon..sun>:HH:MM, or an interval such as 15m, 2h, 1d (interval:<minutes> also works).

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone the cron / time of day is in.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: The inputs every scheduled run gets.

task.title: Task
task.description: What the skill does, in plain words, e.g. 'Search for dentists in Austin and list them'.

start_url.title: Start Url
start_url.description: The page the skill starts on (http/https).

name.title: Name
name.description: Skill name; derived from the task when omitted.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: The skill's inputs and the example value the recording uses for each, e.g. {"city": "Austin"}. Each value must appear in what the browser types or opens, so a later run can swap in its own. Inferred from the task when omitted.

output_fields.title: Output Fields
output_fields.description: The columns each row returns, as {name: description} or a list of names, e.g. ["name", "rating", "phone"]. Inferred from the task when omitted.

login_id.title: Login Id
login_id.description: Your saved login (POST /v1/logins) for a start page behind a sign-in. The recording browser signs in with it first, and the new skill is bound to it so every run signs in the same way.

CreateSkillRequest.title: CreateSkillRequest
CreateSkillRequest.description: What the caller wants the skill to do, and where it starts.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: The inputs a run takes (the API trigger): [{name, type, required, default, description, example}]; type is string, number, integer, boolean, array or object.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The steps, in the same JSON the app saves: [{id, name, type, config, on_error, retries}]. type is one of the executor's step types (skill, workflow, http, code, transform, agent, ...). A skill step names the skill in config.skill; a workflow step in config.target_workflow_id. Steps read inputs as {{inputs.<name>}}.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Edges between steps: [{from_step, to_step}]. Leave empty for a straight line (steps run in order).

workspace_id.title: Workspace Id
workspace_id.description: A workspace you belong to; default your personal workspace.

balance.title: Balance
balance.description: Credits you can spend now, exact to 0.01 (a decimal string).

balance_number.title: Balance Number
balance_number.description: The same balance as a number.

topup_credits.title: Topup Credits
topup_credits.description: Of the balance: credits bought as top-ups.

low.title: Low
low.description: True when the balance is under low_threshold — runs stop at 0.

missing_fields.title: Missing Fields
missing_fields.description: Contract fields fewer than half the rows came back with.

partial_fields.title: Partial Fields
partial_fields.description: Fields filled on at least half the rows but not all, whose blank rows the page capture explained (see per_field severity/note).

per_field.title: Per Field
per_field.description: Every field some rows lacked: fill, where it was tried, evidence.

triage_kind.title: Triage Kind
triage_kind.description: missing_fields | partial_fields | not_shown | suspect_rows | element_changed | extraction_drift | blocked | logged_out | login_failed | site_down | page_not_loaded | recording_failed | unknown

quality_flags.title: Quality Flags
quality_flags.description: Single-run row checks that fired: repeated rows, pages repeating earlier pages, placeholder values.

no_real_rows.title: No Real Rows
no_real_rows.description: Rows came back but every field was empty on every one — the run never reached the results.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One readable line, e.g. 'phone: found on 0/5 rows — tried the result cards'.

Diagnosis.title: Diagnosis
Diagnosis.description: Why the run came back short, and what a hint could say to fix it (POST /v1/skills/{slug}/improve).

skill_id.title: Skill Id
skill_id.description: The ID of the skill to execute

browser_type.title: Browser Type
browser_type.description: Browser mode for THIS run: remote | extension | local_profile | none. Omit to use the skill's saved browser_type (falling back to 'remote').

proxy_config.title: Proxy Config
proxy_config.description: Regional proxy for THIS run (country code / 'random' / 'none'). Omit to use the skill's saved proxy_config.

max_pages.title: Max Pages
max_pages.description: Page ceiling for paginated skills: None = recipe default, 0 = all pages.

scrape_mode.title: Scrape Mode
scrape_mode.description: Scrape mode for THIS run (bridge skills): 'deep' (careful replay) | 'flash' (fast reveal sweep; falls back to deep when degraded). Omit to use the skill's saved scrape_mode (falling back to 'deep').

ExecuteSkillRequest.title: ExecuteSkillRequest
ExecuteSkillRequest.description:
Request to execute a skill.

User-friendly request format.

filled.title: Filled
filled.description: Rows that got the field, e.g. '0/5'.

where_tried.title: Where Tried
where_tried.description: Where the recipe looked, e.g. 'the result cards', "each row's details page".

not_shown.title: Not Shown
not_shown.description: Blank rows whose result card shows no value for the field at all (e.g. a sponsored card) — not a read the skill missed. Null when it could not be told.

shown_unread.title: Shown Unread
shown_unread.description: Blank rows whose result card DOES show a value — a read the skill missed. Set on partial fields (filled on at least half the rows) the page capture could speak for.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Partial fields only: warn (on the card but not read on some rows — a hint can fix it) | info (the blank rows' cards show no value — nothing to fix).

note.title: Note
note.description: Partial fields only, e.g. 'filled on 3/5 — on the card but not read on 2' or 'filled on 3/5 — not shown on 2 rows' cards'.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: fix: fill fields the skill misses, from a hint about where the data is (the default). add_fields: capture NEW fields described in plain English. relearn_details: rebuild how the skill clicks into each result (its per-row detail steps) — for a site that changed or detail fields that come back empty.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.description: fix: what the skill gets wrong and where the data really is, e.g. 'The phone is on the details page — click the place name, the panel opens, the number is next to the phone icon.' add_fields: the new fields, e.g. 'also capture the star rating and the review count'. relearn_details: an optional note, e.g. 'the details now open in a side panel'. Required (3+ characters) for fix, and for add_fields unless fields names them.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: fix: the output fields the hint is about (e.g. ["phone"]); omit to use the fields the last run came back without, or the ones the hint names. add_fields: the new fields' names, when you know them. relearn_details: only re-learn these detail fields.

example_input.title: Example Input
example_input.description: Inputs for the check run (max 5 rows) that proves the improvement. Omit to use the skill's recorded example.

browser_type.title: Browser Type
browser_type.description: The browser to learn and check on: remote (cloud browser) | extension (your Chrome). Omit to use the browser the skill normally runs on (its saved browser mode, else remote). A skill that runs in your Chrome needs the extension connected.

ImproveSkillRequest.title: ImproveSkillRequest
ImproveSkillRequest.description: What to change, in plain English, the way you would coach a person doing the task.

browser_type.title: Browser Type
browser_type.description: The browser it learned and checked on: remote | extension

ImprovementDetails.title: ImprovementDetails
ImprovementDetails.description:
What the engine made of the words: for add_fields, the request diffed against the
skill's contract (genuinely new fields, re-worded duplicates merged into an existing field,
ones it could not place, asked back as a question); and what the learn pass did.

recorded_value.title: Recorded Value
recorded_value.description: The value the recording typed or opened that this input replaces on each run. It must appear in the recipe. Without it the input is added but changes nothing yet.

rename.title: Rename
rename.description: New name; every use in the recipe is renamed too

default.title: Default
default.description: New default; null clears it (the input becomes required)

remove.title: Remove
remove.description: Names to remove; refused while the recipe uses one

site.title: Site
site.description: The site's domain or URL, e.g. example.com.

totp_secret.title: Totp Secret
totp_secret.description: Authenticator seed (base32 or otpauth:// URI) when the site asks for an app code.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as ?cursor= for the next page; null on the last page.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: True when there is a next page (next_cursor is not null).

LoginOut.title: LoginOut
LoginOut.description: A saved login as every caller sees it: never the password, seed or a code.

LoginUpdate.title: LoginUpdate
LoginUpdate.description: Every field optional; given ones replace the stored value. totp_secret "" removes it.

rename.title: Rename
rename.description: New name; its key is renamed in the recipe too

ParameterType.title: ParameterType
ParameterType.description: Supported parameter types for skill inputs.

monthly_allowance.title: Monthly Allowance
monthly_allowance.description: Credits the plan adds each month.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: fail (the output is not data; a validation rejects it) | warn

QualityFlag.title: QualityFlag
QualityFlag.description: A single-run row check that fired (row_checks.py).

code.title: Code
code.description: The sign-in code the site sent.

RunStatusResponse.title: RunStatusResponse
RunStatusResponse.description: GET /v1/runs/{run_id}: status while it runs, the result once it is done.

RunSummary.title: RunSummary
RunSummary.description: The last finished run of a skill or workflow, as a list row shows it.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: The workflow's inputs (see input_schema on GET /v1/workflows/{slug}).

wait.title: Wait
wait.description: /run only: seconds to wait for the result (default 60, max 120). Still running then → 202 with run_id and status_url.

webhook_url.title: Webhook Url

SkillImprovementStatus.title: SkillImprovementStatus
SkillImprovementStatus.description:
Where an improvement is: queued → working → validating → done | failed.

``done`` with ``improved: true`` means the new recipe version is live; ``done`` with
``improved: false`` means the attempt was kept as a candidate version (not live) and
``outcome`` says why. ``failed`` means the engine could not run (``error``). ``result``
says the same in one word.
